subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - next steps
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity SLOs / next steps

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align on the validation window. Our goals from the call:
- Target p95 latency <= 200ms for short-chat generation (<= 256 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: ~120 requests/sec (avg payload ~120 tokens) with burst up to 250 rps during peak.
- Concurrency: support 16 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions (server-sent events style) with progressive partial tokens.
- Model: plan to run an open 70B model (we're evaluating a quantized FP16 runtime).

Questions we need you to confirm:
1) Recommended GPU type(s) for baseline + cost-effective option (we mentioned H100 vs A100 vs L4 on the call).
2) How reserved throughput maps to GPUs (i.e., how many rtx/gpu equivalents for 120 rps).
3) Any expected difference in streaming latency vs non-streaming for the same throughput, and guidance to hit p95 200ms.
4) What telemetry and logs you need from our side to run the validation tests (sample payloads, keys, IP allowlist).

Happy to kick off a 1-week validation window next week if we can get a short test plan and an estimate. Also copying ops as they'll run the load harness.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jensen
CTO, Acme Corp
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity performance validation - next steps

Hi Sara — great talking earlier. Recap + proposed plan below so we have a single source of truth: 

Recap of SLOs (as we heard them):
- p95 latency target: <= 200ms for <=256-token responses.
- Sustained throughput: 120 rps (avg 120 tokens).
- Burst: up to 250 rps for short windows (~5 minutes).
- Concurrency: 16 streaming sessions with low-latency chunk delivery.

Proposed validation plan (1-week window):
1) Baseline profiling (2 days): we run microbenchmarks on H100, A100, and L4 variants with your sample workload (you provide payloads). Goal: pick representative instance sizes.
2) Load test (2 days): run steady-state load @120 rps for 4–6 hours, plus 2 burst windows at 250 rps. Measure p50/p95/p99, tail latency, and streaming chunk latency.
3) Stability (2 days): 24-hour soak at 120 rps to ensure KV cache/GC behaviors.
4) Post-test analysis (1 day): deliver results + recommended Dedicated capacity sizing and a short SLA draft.

Quick answers to your questions:
1) GPU recommendations:
   - Baseline (performance): H100 (larger fp16 throughput, lower latency for 70B).
   - Cost-effective: A100 if you can tolerate slightly higher p95, or L4 for smaller quantized variants where throughput needs are modest.
   - We'll provide concrete per-GPU estimated rps for your profile after baseline profiling.
2) Reserved throughput mapping: we map reserved throughput to "reserved request units" backed by GPU capacity. Early estimate: an H100 can sustain ~200-300 rps for short-chat style at 70B fp16 depending on batch/kv cache; we will confirm with the microbench.
3) Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming adds ~10–40ms per-chunk overhead depending on network and chunk size. We'll instrument chunk latency separately so you can see the streaming tail.
4) Telemetry: sample payloads (JSON), a small set of test API keys (we'll use a short-lived token), and a list of source IPs for allowlisting.

Next steps:
- Sara: share sample payloads + ops contact for test harness.
- Acme ops: share IP allowlist and preferred start date (we're proposing Wed 2/18).
- Redwood: Rafael will share an initial sizing estimate and test harness instructions (attached test results from our internal sim).

Attaching: basic internal perf sim output (we'll expand this after profiling).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity performance validation - initial sizing

Hi team — attaching a quick set of initial numbers from our lab runs (see attachment load_test_results_v1.csv). High-level notes:

- Model profile: 70B dense fp16, average output 120 tokens, request size ~120 tokens.
- H100 (1x): baseline single-GPU observed ~180–250 rps for short-chat with batching; p95 ~90–160ms in ideal batch conditions.
- A100 (1x): ~140–200 rps; p95 ~120–220ms depending on batching and KV cache hit rate.
- L4 (1x): ~60–90 rps for this model size; best when using a quantized 4-bit path and shorter responses.

Recommendations for your SLOs (p95 <= 200ms, 120 rps sustained, 16 streaming sessions):
- Option A (recommended for headroom): 2x H100 reserved (gives comfortable headroom for 120 rps + bursts; burst to 250 rps uses autoscaling/burst capacity).
- Option B (cost-balanced): 2x A100 + aggressive KV cache tuning and batching; p95 may approach target under heavy burst unless we increase reserved units.
- Option C (cost-minimal): 4x L4 with a quantized model variant but expect longer development effort for quantization and likely degraded quality.

Notes on streaming: H100 gave best streaming chunk latency; on A100 we saw slightly higher per-chunk jitter. We recommend configuring chunk size ~64 tokens to minimize per-chunk overhead.

Telemetry & test harness: we need a small sample dataset (50-100 representative requests) and a short-lived API key. Please confirm where to upload (we can use the Drive link Aditya shared).

I'll be on the validation run next week and will share an expanded CSV after the baseline profiling.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
